mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Passport (each shareholder and director)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport Office / Notary Public in country of origin

Bank reference letter covering at least 2 years of banking relationship

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and beneficial owners against Samoa FIU sanctions lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database. Enhanced due diligence required for PEPs, with approval by the Money Laundering Compliance Officer of the licensed registered agent.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Companies Registry, Online Name Reservation System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in either English or Samoan. Roman alphabet mandatory. Non-Latin scripts are transliterated phonetically into English/Samoan. Any foreign-language name requires a certified English translation and must be available in the Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of rejection, requesting reconsideration with a legal argument and supporting evidence. If the Registrar maintains rejection, the applicant may appeal to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within a further 30 days, and ultimately to the Supreme Court of Samoa by way of judicial review. Name reservations may be extended for one additional 30-day period upon payment of a renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office acceptance is conditional. For a low-risk SaaS holding entity, a licensed registered agent may provide a registered office address that includes a physical Samoa street address and a physical mail-receiving point. Pure 'hot-desk' virtual offices without a dedicated physical suite are not permitted for International Companies.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 10%) – unannounced physical inspections are triggered by AML risk flags, complaints, or statistical sampling, but may occur at the discretion of the Registrar and the Financial Intelligence Unit.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 2016 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2023; ss. 5 (method of incorporation), 9 (memorandum and articles), 36 (registered office and registered agent), 144 (exemption from domestic licensing)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - Registry of International Companies, Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Application for Registration of an International Company, together with the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; incorporation is permitted with nil issued capital and no escrow, bank deposit, or capital verification requirement (s. 12, International Companies Act 2016).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscribers' subscriptions for 1,000 ordinary shares of USD 1.00 each, fully paid, are approved, allotted, and recorded in the register of members; (2) the registered office is fixed at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, who is authorized to file all statutory notices with SIFA; (3) [Name A], [Name B], and [Name C] are appointed as Directors until the next annual general meeting; (4) [Name D] is appointed as Corporate Secretary; and (5) the Directors are authorized to open bank accounts, appoint a US registered agent, and execute all documents necessary to establish the Company's email newsletter infrastructure operations and payment processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - Name Registry Desk / electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application for the proposed international company name (e.g., '[Client] Email Infra Ltd.') together with a comparable-names search. The name must not conflict with any name already registered in Samoa, must not be misleading, and must end with 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation. SIFA issues a name reservation certificate valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Copy of passport of each proposed director/shareholder
Registered agent engagement letter confirming name availability check
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity or undesirability, file a revised name application with a letter of consent from the existing name holder or appeal to the Registrar within 14 days under s. 14 of the International Companies Act 2016.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent (SIFA-approved) and Samoa Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association under the International Companies Act 2016, providing for no-par or par-value ordinary shares, permitted objects encompassing SaaS and email infrastructure services, and a board of not fewer than one director. The subscribers execute the memorandum and articles before a notary public; the registered agent countersigns Form 1 and files the statutory declaration of compliance with the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director (each proposed director)
Subscriber due diligence pack (passport, proof of address, bank reference)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Form 1 or constitutional documents are deficient, correct and resubmit through the registered agent within 30 days; cure of incomplete statement of compliance is effected by filing a supplementary declaration and paying the prescribed refiling fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission to SIFA and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - Registry of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Form 1, Memorandum and Articles of Association, director consents, and declaration of compliance via the SIFA client portal administrated by the registered agent or in person at SIFA offices in Apia. Pay the government incorporation fee of USD 200 plus the registered agent arrangement fee. Where transaction timetables require acceleration, request express processing for same-day or next-day certification.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for incomplete or inconsistent particulars, file a supplementary return with correcting details within 14 days; SIFA reissues the certificate upon satisfaction without requiring a fresh application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation with a unique registration number; the company is constituted from the date stated on the certificate. The registered agent obtains a certified copy, updates the statutory registers (members, directors, charges, and beneficial ownership), and issues the corporate kit.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of legalized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statutory registers opened by the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the certificate is issued with clerical error, apply to the Registrar for rectification under s. 26 of the Act; the Registrar may issue an amended certificate without prejudice to third-party rights.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent / Corporate Secretary and First Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the First Board of Directors meeting (by written consent or virtual attendance) to adopt the First Board Resolution approving share issuance, fixing the registered office, appointing officers, and authorizing banking and payment-rail contracts (Stripe Billing and credit card acquiring). Prepare executed minutes, open the corporate bank account with a licensed international bank in Apia, and file the resolution with the registered agent for the statutory records.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (signed minutes or unanimous written consent)
Share certificates and register of members
Bank account opening package (certificate of incorporation, resolution, KYC documents)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If banking or payment processors require additional corporate good standing evidence, obtain a Certificate of Good Standing from SIFA within 2 business days. Any defect in the resolution is cured by a unanimous written consent signed by all directors and filed with the registered agent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) - Business Licence Division (domestic licensing regime; International Companies are expressly exempt under s. 144, International Companies Act 2016, provided no business is conducted with Samoan residents)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required - the Certificate of Incorporation issued by SIFA constitutes the sole operating authorization for the offshore delivery of email newsletter infrastructure services. A domestic 'Business Licence' under the Business Licences Act 1998 (Samoa) is not applicable to an International Company transacting exclusively outside Samoa.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity (hosted transactional email API and newsletter platform) is a purely digital service with no physical land use, construction, or manufacturing footprint within Samoa; no EIA application, preliminary assessment, or registration is triggered under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, hazardous waste generation, or physical effluents arising in Samoa. Compute and data-storage operations are hosted on third-party cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS, Google Cloud) governed by the environmental compliance regimes of their own jurisdictions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable - the company maintains no employee workplace, leased premises, or physical installation in Samoa. Should a representative office subsequently be opened in Apia, prior fire-safety certification from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA), building occupancy clearance from the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI), and a domestic employment registration would be required; no such clearances are triggered for a pure offshore operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of the Independent State of Samoa (Matagaluega o Tupe Maua), online portal: Ministry for Revenue Online Services at https://www.revenue.gov.ws (successor to the former Samoa Revenue Authority; tax administration unified at national level with no sub-national tax authorities).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned entity must be incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 (ICA 1987) through a licensed Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) registered agent, obtaining a Certificate of Incorporation and, where sought, a Certificate of Tax Exemption under ICA 1987. The entity then files a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) application with the Ministry for Revenue using Form IRD-001 (Application for Registration), accompanied by: (1) certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation; (2) Memorandum and Articles of Association; (3) SIFA-issued good standing certificate; (4) certified passport copies of directors/shareholders; (5) registered agent details and Samoa registered office address; and (6) a non-resident status declaration. The TIN is typically issued within 3 to 5 business days. If the International Company (IC) expects to make taxable supplies with a Samoa nexus exceeding SAT 100,000 in any consecutive 12-month period, the same form triggers compulsory Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration; the IC may also voluntarily register for GST to recover input tax on local administrative costs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone. An International Company incorporated under the ICA 1987 is a non-resident, non-domestic entity subject to entity-level tax exemption: it is exempt from Samoa income tax, withholding tax, stamp duty, and all other national taxes on its international business income and transactions, provided it does not carry on business with Samoa residents, own Samoa land (except under a licensed international scheme), or derive income from Samoa sources. For GST purposes the IC remains within the territorial scope only for supplies connected with Samoa; offshore SaaS exports are treated as exported services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no US-style check-the-box or look-through election for ICs. Available statutory mechanisms: (a) ICA 1987 s.195 election: an IC may apply to the Minister for Revenue to be treated as a resident company for purposes of a double taxation agreement, thereby becoming subject to Samoa income tax on its worldwide income to the extent required for treaty benefits; (b) GST voluntary registration election under Goods and Services Tax Act 2017 (GST Act 2017) s.16, available to any person making taxable supplies regardless of turnover; (c) conversion election under ICA 1987 Part VIII to re-domicile as a domestic Samoa company, which terminates the Tax_Exempt_Zone status; (d) no hybrid mismatch election is prescribed under Samoa law, and the Income Tax Ordinance 2015 applies a general anti-avoidance rule and principal purpose test (with OECD BEPS-aligned rules) to deny treaty or exemption benefits where there is an abusive hybrid arrangement.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (GST/VAGST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 2017 (administered by the Ministry for Revenue)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT 100,000 of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period (mandatory registration); voluntary registration is available below the threshold; non-resident International Companies are only within the registration net for supplies with a Samoa nexus, and exported services do not count toward the threshold unless the IC is registered voluntarily.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, API-based continuous transaction control, or digital stamping regime operates in Samoa. Tax invoices may be issued in paper or electronic format; a GST-registered supplier must issue a tax invoice within 28 days of a taxable supply, and an electronic invoicing system may be used only with prior approval of the Commissioner of the Ministry for Revenue. In practice, email-infrastructure SaaS providers use standard billing systems (e.g., Stripe Billing) without statutory data integration obligations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% GST) is available under GST Act 2017 for the export of goods and the export of services. For a bulk transactional email API and newsletter hosting platform, the relevant criterion is the 'exported services' rule: the services are supplied to a recipient who is outside Samoa and not in Samoa at the time of supply; the services are not directly connected with land or goods situated in Samoa; and the services are not supplied to a person carrying on a business in Samoa to the extent the supply relates to that Samoa business. Offshore recipients of email infrastructure services therefore qualify for the 0% rate, enabling the IC to claim input tax credits/refunds on Samoa-sourced purchases (agent fees, local office costs, hosting expenses in Samoa) attributable to the zero-rated exports. If the IC is not GST-registered, exports fall outside the scope of Samoa GST with no refund entitlement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CusDec/EEZI) validated by the Samoa Customs Service — applicable to tangible goods; for pure email SaaS services no customs declaration is required and a written declaration of service export is used
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of goods (not applicable to services; replaced by service delivery records and API/session logs)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT credit advice from a licensed Samoa commercial bank evidencing receipt of foreign currency export proceeds
Commercial Invoice and executed customer contract/order form identifying the non-resident recipient, description of email/newsletter hosting services, and currency of settlement

Recipient non-residency proof: certificate of residence/tax residence, jurisdiction of incorporation, and IP/domain registration data corroborating offshore consumption of the email infrastructure services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Commissioner may audit exporters within the statutory record-keeping period (5 years) and issue a default assessment or raise a retrospective GST clawback where zero-rating is not supported by contemporaneous export documentation. Fraudulent or reckless zero-rating claims attract: (a) a tax shortfall penalty of up to 200% of the tax evaded or a fixed penalty not exceeding SAT 50,000 for companies, at the Commissioner's discretion; (b) late payment interest at a statutory rate (CBS reference rate plus margin, currently yielding approximately 10% p.a.) running from the original due date; (c) criminal liability including fines up to SAT 100,000 and imprisonment for up to 5 years for knowing misrepresentation or aiding GST evasion; and (d) suspension or cancellation of GST registration and loss of input credit entitlement. All export substantiation documents must be retained for 5 years, and failure to repatriate export proceeds within 90 days without Central Bank of Samoa approval may additionally trigger exchange control penalties and de-registration of the exporter.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) and the Ministry of Finance Exchange Control Division, operating under the Exchange Control Act 1972 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1972
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa has accepted Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement, guaranteeing unrestricted current-account payments and transfers without the need for Central Bank approval. The national currency is the Samoan tala (WST), managed through a trade-weighted basket of NZD, AUD, USD, and JPY. Onshore resident entities remain subject to certain capital-account exchange controls and documentary requirements. However, an International Company (IC) registered under the International Companies Act 1987 is statutorily designated as non-resident for exchange-control purposes. Accordingly, the IC may maintain all treasury assets in USD, EUR, or other global currencies; may make dividend, loan, and liquidation remittances to non-resident shareholders without WST conversion; and is not subject to the onshore profit-remittance licensing procedure. Practical profit-remittance hurdles are minimal: banks will require an up-to-date Certificate of Good Standing, a tax exemption certificate, and a board resolution authorizing the remittance for amounts exceeding USD 10,000 or equivalent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For resident Samoan onshore exporters, the CBS Exchange Control Regulations impose a mandatory surrender rule: 100% of export proceeds in foreign currency must be offered for sale to an authorized commercial bank and converted into Samoan tala within 90 days of receipt unless a formal exemption certificate is issued by the CBS. International Companies (ICs) are expressly carved out from this regime due to their non-resident status under the Exchange Control Act. Consequently, all export receipts and recurring subscription revenue derived from the email newsletter platform (e.g., wholesale Stripe Billing payouts) may be retained indefinitely in foreign currency with no mandatory conversion ratio and no forced deposit into a Samoan tala account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (Samoa) Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-Low. The Central Bank of Samoa licenses electronic money institutions under the Non-Bank Financial Institutions Act 2019, but only where a physical presence or a sponsored in-country agent is established. Fully remote offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) can provide auxiliary US/UK/EU payment collection in the same settlement vertical, but are not authorized to clear payments in Samoan tala and are subject to the CBS's inbound cross-border payment monitoring. For this commercial model, the recommended legal structure is to retain Stripe Billing as the primary card-acquiring rail, with payouts settled into the IC's USD account at a Samoa tier-1 bank. Any offshore EMI used only as an interim collection pool should maintain balances below the local licensing threshold and should not be represented to customers as the official treasury account holder.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Samoa's tier-1 commercial banks require at least one authorized director and the registered agent/subscriber to attend a physical KYC interview at the Apia head office before the account can be opened. A hybrid remote-opening protocol exists: the director may appear via video conference with a certified passport, a digital identity verification report, and a notarized power of attorney naming the Samoa licensed registered agent as the on-site sponsor. The local agent will countersign the bank's KYC pack and physically verify the original documents. Second signatories can be onboarded entirely remotely using apostilled documents and a bank reference from a principal banking relationship outside Samoa. Overall, a full virtual account opening without any physical presence is not currently available under the CBS prudential guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived lack of economic substance because the IC is tax-exempt and has only a registered office address in Apia
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract from the Samoa Registry confirming incorporation; Certificate of Good Standing; registered agent service agreement; substance declaration confirming that board resolutions, bank signatory instructions, treasury policy manual, and accounting records are physically stored in Samoa; ongoing annual filing receipts; and a notarized statement from the local compliance officer that the IC is managed and controlled in Samoa.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer share or anonymous nominee ownership structure historically associated with offshore IBCs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate confirming the IC has no bearer shares and only registered shares; full chain-of-title of the share capital; complete beneficial ownership schedule with natural-person names, passports, residential addresses, and proof of the investor's source of wealth; audited financial statements or certified management accounts for the last two years; and a copy of the shareholders' register authenticated by the registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bulk email newsletter hosting platform is perceived as a potential vector for spam, phishing, or payment-card fraud
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Technical governance dossier containing: a platform demo and architecture diagram; the subscription and consent-flow description; industry credentials such as SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001, or PCI DSS Level 1; current sanitized subscriber statistics; sample commercial contracts with established downstream customers; a written AML/CTF risk assessment for the platform; and a compliance attestation confirming the platform's automated abuse detection and takedown policies for fraudulent payment activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections must be routed using a compliant SWIFT MT103 wire transfer from the shareholder's bank to the IC's USD-denominated account at a Samoa licensed bank. The remittance instruction must include a clear purpose code, typically referenced as 'Equity capital for the purchase of issued shares' (Samoa BOP classification code S100), and must cite the board resolution date approving the share issuance in field 70 of the MT103. The receiving bank will require a board resolution, an updated shareholder register, and the completed 'Customer Source of Funds Declaration' to evidence the lawful origin of the funds. Because the IC is non-resident for exchange-control purposes, the capital injection remains in USD and is not converted into WST; however, the bank is obligated to report the transaction to the CBS for balance-of-payments statistics. If the capital injection transits through an offshore fintech EMI, the EMI's name must match the shareholder name exactly; otherwise the bank will reject the credit for compliance review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operational trade disbursements the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103, used for cloud-infrastructure vendor payments (AWS, DigitalOcean), SaaS licensing fees, professional advisory invoices, and dividend distributions. Each outbound MT103 must be encoded with the correct beneficiary bank identifier (BIC), an IBAN or US ABA account number where applicable, and a statement in field 70 including the invoice and commercial contract reference. For low-value monthly disbursements, an automatic clearing house (ACH) tokenized payment within a United States treasury pool may be linked to the same Samoa bank account, provided the bank has an executed ACH relationship with its US correspondent. Commercial letters of credit (LC) are not necessary for this software business model, but a standby letter of credit (SBLC) can be established at the tier-1 Samoan bank to secure a material datacenter or hardware supply agreement if and when capital expenditure increases; documentary collections (D/P and D/A) may be used for single large-scale hardware purchases, though market practice favors straightforward SWIFT wires for SaaS disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward foreign exchange contracts (FX forwards) on USD/WST and USD/EUR with an authorized Samoan commercial bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the Samoan tala where offshore liquidity is insufficient or where the underlying exposure is an accounting-only translation risk
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for intercompany treasury structures involving long-term USD to EUR or USD to AUD funding arrangements
European-style foreign exchange options (plain vanilla calls and puts) transacted under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with bank counterparties rated at or above Standard & Poor's A-
FX swaps for short-term operational rollover between USD, EUR, and WST once the Samoan bank confirms pricing under a global treasury limit

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government License Renewal Fee (Samoa International Company annual government charge)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) via licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable annually on the incorporation anniversary; remitted to the Registrar within 30 days of the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% per annum late-fee accrual on overdue amount; continued default beyond 6-12 months exposes the company to administrative strike-off order by the Registrar without court proceedings, followed by asset vesting in the Crown

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form IC-AR) confirming registered details, shareholding, directors, and registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour / SIFA, submitted by the registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed yearly within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation and in any case before the annual fee due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate WST late-filing penalty; default triggers presumption of non-good standing and may lead to administrative strike-off after statutory notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT client-due-diligence refresh declaration provided to the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent subject to SIFA AML Rules; no direct submission to the Financial Intelligence Unit by a non-reporting exempt-zone company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed on each material change in beneficial ownership and on a reasonable annual cycle where there are active transactions or share transfers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Agent may freeze files and refuse to process payments while KYC refresh is outstanding; persistent failure can trigger agent resignation and Registrar strike-off proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory external audit for a standard Samoa International Company with no trust, banking, or financial-services license; audit may be triggered by the Articles/Constitution, a shareholder requisition typically 25% or more, or a license condition imposed by SIFA
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies must maintain books enabling true and fair accounts; IFRS or US GAAP is accepted; financial statements are not filed with the Registrar and remain confidential

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Samoa maintains central UBO registers for domestic companies only; an International Company is not publicly registered by UBO, but the licensed agent must record and annually re-confirm beneficial ownership under SIFA AML Rules, with an immediate update on each share transfer
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Directors and Shareholders Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500-5,000 per audit engagement (only when triggered by shareholder or license requirement)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for International Company (IC) — s.195 International Companies Act 1987 grants full exemption; general Samoa corporate income tax rate is 25% for resident trading companies (Income Tax Act 1974).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Permanent statutory tax holiday: no income tax, no capital gains tax, no stamp duty, no exchange-control levy on the IC's income, assets, or transactions; dividends paid to shareholders are statutorily exempt. No income tax registration or annual tax return is required for a pure offshore IC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return — IC Form AR-1; submitted electronically by the licensed Samoa Registered Agent via the MCIL/SIFA Registrar of International Companies platform
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 60 calendar days after the anniversary of incorporation (International Companies Act 1987, s.140); no extension is prescribed by statute.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal company name and IC registry number as per the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may not alter the registered name except by special resolution lodged through the licensed Samoa registered agent.
The incorporation anniversary controls the filing deadline; non-resident owners must calendar the date to avoid strike-off while operating offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered Office and licensed Registered Agent particulars (physical Samoa address).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A post-office box or virtual offshore address is insufficient; the agent must be a licensed Samoa registered agent under the International Companies Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized share capital and currency denomination.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum paid-up capital applies; capital may be denominated in any freely convertible currency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issued share capital and classes of shares in issue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident persons may hold all issued shares; bearer shares, where in issue, must remain in the custody of the Samoa registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Register of Members — shareholder names, addresses, share classes, and holdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide country of residence, passport or entity registration identification, and share details; beneficial owners must be separately disclosed to the registered agent under AML/CFT rules and need not appear in the public register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors and Secretary — full names, nationalities, residential addresses, and identification documents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No Samoa residency requirement applies; at least one director is required and may be a body corporate; identification documents must be held by the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compliance declaration (solvency, confirmation of no domestic Samoa business) and payment of annual licence fee.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration may be signed by a director or by the registered agent under a power of attorney; false certification is a criminal offense.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of WST 100 per month (or part thereof) plus 10% per annum late-payment interest on the annual licence fee; default exceeding 6 months triggers administrative strike-off and loss of legal capacity; reinstatement requires settlement of all arrears and penalties plus a Registrar or court order.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return — NOT APPLICABLE; a pure International Company must not register with the Samoa Ministry of Revenue (CIT portal: nil registration).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: None — an IC is outside the Samoa corporate income tax net under s.195 International Companies Act 1987; if inadvertently issued a Samoan tax file number, file a final nil return or apply for deregistration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nil CIT Return — the exempt IC has no assessable income, no allowable deductions, and no tax payable; financial records (IFRS or equivalent) must nevertheless be maintained in Samoa via the registered agent for economic-substance verification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must ensure global email-infrastructure SaaS revenue is not attributed to a Samoa permanent establishment and must not hold Samoa-source domestic customer contracts; obtain a written tax opinion before onboarding Samoa-resident clients.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: No CIT penalty applies to a correctly structured exempt IC; loss of exemption through local trading triggers default assessment at 25% corporate tax, 25% penalty tax, 2% monthly late-payment interest, and a fine of up to WST 100,000 for failure to furnish a return.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — dividends, distributions, and deemed distributions paid by an International Company to non-resident or resident shareholders are statutorily exempt (s.195 ICA 1987). For comparison, Samoa's general statutory dividend WHT on a resident trading company is 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No DTA claim is necessary while the IC exemption applies. Where residual WHT arises (e.g., a Samoan resident payer of an IC-related fee), the beneficial owner must: (1) obtain a Samoa Certificate of Residence from the Ministry of Revenue; (2) submit the certificate and a DTA relief form to the withholding payer before settlement; (3) certify beneficial ownership of the income stream; and (4) retain all supporting documentation for five years. Samoa's DTAs with New Zealand and Australia generally cap dividends at 5%-15%, interest at 10%, and royalties at 10%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: IC outbound royalty and interest: 0% statutory exemption. General Samoa statutory WHT: 15% on royalties and 15% on interest paid to non-residents; DTA rates with New Zealand and Australia typically 10% on both, subject to beneficial-ownership certification.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No WST-denominated threshold is enacted: Samoa has not adopted OECD Local File / Master File or CbCR filing legislation for International Companies. The general anti-avoidance rule in the Income Tax Act 1974 permits the Commissioner to recharacterize non-arm's-length related-party pricing. All intercompany contracts (email platform licence fees, API infrastructure charges, management fees) must therefore be supported by documented arm's-length pricing and contemporary evidence of Samoa substance.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2021 and its 2022 Regulations subject an IC to Economic Substance Requirements when it carries on a 'relevant activity' — including Headquarters, Distribution and Service Centre, Financing, and IP Holding — from Samoa. A Bulk Transactional Email API and Newsletter Hosting Platform (ISIC 6201, NAICS 518210) supplying related parties will be scrutinized as a service-centre / headquarters activity; the IC must evidence: (i) physical premises in Samoa; (ii) adequate full-time employees; (iii) proportionate local operating expenditure; and (iv) board meetings directed and managed in Samoa. A passive foreign-owned IC serving unrelated global customers must still maintain substance-consistent records but faces a lower factual ESR burden.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Abuse of IC Exempt Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Carrying on trade within Samoa with Samoa residents or deriving Samoa-source income while holding the IC as an offshore billing front, thereby automatically forfeiting the s.195 exemption and triggering full corporate tax exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment at the 25% corporate rate on deemed Samoa profits, 25% penalty tax, 2% per month late-payment interest, a 5-year back-duty window, and a fine of up to WST 100,000 under the Income Tax Act 1974.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the certified unpaid tax (s.132 ITA 1974); fraudulent evasion carries imprisonment up to 7 years; the court may issue travel bans and freeze personal assets pending prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining zero or sham substance in Samoa — no office, no employees, board meetings conducted offshore, or filing a false annual economic-substance declaration for the email infrastructure entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to WST 1,000,000 under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2021; persistent violation for 12+ months triggers compulsory strike-off by the Registrar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced: each director is personally liable for the fine; making a false substance declaration is an indictable offense punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years; travel bans and asset preservation orders commonly accompany enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the transactional email API without CDD on beneficial owners, processing payments for phishing/spam campaigns through the Stripe billing rails, or failing to file a Suspicious Transaction Report with the Samoa FIU.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Samoa AML/CFT Act 2007: corporate fine up to WST 2,000,000; money-laundering conviction: imprisonment up to 10 years and asset confiscation under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2007; failure to report a suspicious transaction: fine up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are prosecuted as natural persons — imprisonment up to 10 years for laundering proceeds derived from fraud; personal assets restrained and forfeited; FIU-issued travel bans apply from the moment an investigation is opened.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to collect subscription fees while knowingly insolvent, dissipating assets to related parties, or making preferential payments to the parent group in contemplation of liquidation of the newsletter infrastructure company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The court may order the director to make unlimited personal contributions to the company's assets; fraudulent trading carries a fine of up to WST 500,000 under the International Companies Act 1987 and applicable company-law provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil restitution of all misapplied funds, extension of judgment liability to shadow directors of the parent entity, disqualification as a director for up to 10 years, and imprisonment up to 5 years for fraudulent trading.
